newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Foreigners hold 12.1 pct of Tel Aviv-listed equity.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners hold 12.1 pct of Tel Aviv-listed equity.

text.p: Foreign investment in the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange accounted for 12.1 percent of the total registered capital at the end of April, the Bank of Israel said on Thursday.
That compared with 11.6 percent at the end of December but below the 12.6 percent peak reached in February, the central bank said.
However, total registered capital grew to 120.47 billion shekels at the end of April from 98.02 billion shekels at the end of 1996, as share prices rose, the Bank of Israel said.
Foreigners invested heavily in the Israeli share market in January after share prices began rising at the end of 1996, signalling the end of a prolonged slump.

The Bank of Israel said the public accounted for 71.4 percent of the total registered share capital of TASE companies. Mutual funds accounted for 5.3 percent, insurance companies 0.3 percent and provident funds 10.9 percent.
